# harborpilot_client_binding (Resource)

A client: who calls the gateway, under which plan and project, with which limits and trust.

Changes made outside Terraform are detected on refresh and shown as a diff of `spec`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harborpilot_client_binding" "claude_code" {
  name = "alice-claude-code"
  spec = jsonencode({
    display_name     = "Alice's Claude Code"
    owner_kind       = "user"
    owner_id         = "usr_01h..."
    plan_id          = harborpilot_routing_plan.default.id
    project_id       = harborpilot_project.checkout.id
    expected_harness = "claude_code"
    limits           = { requests_per_minute = 120, max_concurrency = 4 }
    trust            = { session_hints = true }
    enabled          = true
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name (lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`).
- `spec` (String) The client binding specification as JSON, usually written with `jsonencode({...})`. See the `BindingSpec` schema in the Harbor Pilot API reference. Properties you leave out are sent as their zero value (empty string, list or map, `0`, `false`), except `enabled`, which must be set.

### Read-Only

- `drift_state` (String) `drifted` when the object was changed outside Terraform since Terraform last wrote it.
- `id` (String) Stable object id.
- `managed_by` (String) Source of the last change (`terraform` after an apply).
- `revision` (Number) Server revision, used for optimistic concurrency.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id or by name.
terraform import harborpilot_client_binding.example <id-or-name>
```
